doc.title: Joe Ascione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

title: Studying with Bernard Purdie
summary: Purdie's teaching style, his advice about keeping the gig, and help setting up a publishing company.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: At the time I was studying too, with Bernard Purdie. And I remember him saying — with Bernard Purdie you sit at the drum set, first of all you can never wear sneakers, he’d throw you out. He always said shoes. And he never played the drums, he would just circle like a shark around the prey. And then he would preach. And he’d come out with these pearls of wisdom every like thirty seconds for an hour. And all of a sudden you’d hear him like, “It’s not getting the gig, it’s keeping the gig.” And he’d stop and he’d start preaching again. And he’d come out with these gems you know. So I remember when I told him I got that gig and he was very excited for me and proud. And he also helped me put together how to secure a publishing company for when you write tunes and to get your foot in the door with a record company, given them one tune and learn the ropes. And so that was a great asset. So yeah, the Fagan thing, it was great.
